tamara: quick sync idea  proposal: unify the routing+auth handshake into a tiny 'session envelope' used by hosted/dedicated/private. keep the envelope minimal: routing hints, an opaque secret_pointer, a negotiation_vector, and very small lease_seconds. avoid inline key material unless the customer explicitly opts in for private installs.

jose: +1 on minimality. One ask: make the secret_pointer permissive in form (kms://, local-path://, token://) so adapters can decide based on trust boundary. Also we need a short list of error outcomes so runtime behavior is deterministic.

liam: We should standardize resolve strategies: early_resolve, on_first_use, external_handshake. Early_resolve is lower latency but requires runtime KMS access; on_first_use is hybrid; external_handshake is for private when customer performs the exchange.

sec-bot: policy: hosted nodes default to no_inline_keys and no external_handshake acceptance. Any exception must be allowlisted with security sign-off. Envelopes must carry audit_nonce and signed_envelope_id.

tamara: Here's an envelope sketch to discuss (compact):
```json
{"envelope_id":"e-9b2","tenant_tag":"hmac-xx","route_hint":"zone-4","secret_pointer":"kms://r/abcd","resolve_strategy":"on_first_use","lease_seconds":240,"negotiation_vector":["resolve_kms","cache_tokens"],"manifest_version":"1"}
```

jose: Unique pieces I'd add: a capability_digest (hash of negotiation_vector) and a fallback_hint (degrade_to_small_model | route_to_fallback_pool | fail). If resolve fails permanently, we follow fallback_hint.

liam: Also need a clear taxonomy for resolve outcomes: RESOLVE_OK, RESOLVE_TEMP_FAIL (retry/backoff), RESOLVE_PERM_FAIL (do not retry), RESOLVE_POLICY_BLOCK (abort + audit). Embedding those outcomes into the spec means higher layers don't guess.

sec-bot: recommend adding telemetry_tag = HMAC(tenant_id, rotate_key) so traces are consistent and irreversible. Also require lease_seconds <= 600 by default.

tamara: Migration corner: when affinity moves mid-session we should issue a short-lived migration envelope with migration_id and grace_seconds so existing cache entries can be revalidated. Without a grace window we'll see huge cache churn.

jose: Implementation note: negotiation step -> control plane issues envelope + allowed_vector; adapter replies with supported_vector and resolve_intent. Control plane compares supports vs allowed. If mismatch, return HANDSHAKE_MISMATCH and fall back to older route.

liam: Private nuance: the envelope MUST NOT contain host-resolvable kms:// URIs. Instead private envelopes use token:// or local-path:// and expect external_handshake. This must be enforced by control plane RBAC.

sec-bot: policy-check queued: enforce no host-kms in private mode, require signed_envelope_id, audit_nonce present. Any policy violation -> envelope rejected.

engops-bot: ci: envelope-schema-tests started, handshake-compat-suite queued.

tamara: action items: jose to draft capability_digest rules and fallback mapping (by Wed), liam to write resolve_outcome enum and runtime handler matrix, sec-bot to formalize private-mode MUST_NOT list. I'll draft the envelope RFC after these are in. If no objections, I'll open PR tomorrow. :thumbsup:

jose: :thumbsup:

liam: +1

sec-bot: policy-note: security review required for any change to default no_inline_keys behavior.
